2026 SEMA Show • Toyota Brings Fresh Adventure-Ready Concepts at the 2026 SEMA Show Under the Woodland Banner
Hybrid Honda Passport Throws More HP in Baja Racing Than Any Other 9.0-Liter V8-Powered Trophy Truck
14 photos
Photo: Honda
Without this being a rule in desert racing, it's not uncommon for the custom, high-performance Trophy Trucks to use massive, 9-liter engines to get them over the many obstacles of such competitions.
On average, these powerplants are capable of developing over 1,000 horsepower, and that makes sense, given their size and fittings. But what if I told you a brand-new Baja truck cranks out much more than that from a 2.4-liter engine and some extras?
The vehicle in question is officially called the Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck, and it was presented by Japanese carmaker Honda just ahead of this year's SEMA show , which opens its doors this week. For all intents and purposes, this is its newest weapon in the fight to land yet another overall Baja 1000 win.
At the heart of the beast is a hybrid powertrain that blends together the merits of a 2.4-liter twin-turbo V6 engine with those of an 800-volt hybrid system. Combined, these bits of hardware should be more than enough to allow the truck to crank out over 1,300 horsepower.
Photo: Honda The vehicle was put together by Honda with assistance from Mason Motorsports, and the engine is not just any other piece of hardware of this kind. I'm talking about an all-aluminum construction based on the engine deployed on the Acura ARX-06 GTP prototype race car, already trialed and tested in some of the world's most demanding competitions, including the Rolex 24 at Daytona and the 12 Hours of Sebring.
Controlling the massive troop is a Masomatic twin-angled drive five-speed transmission put together by Mason Motorsports. Then, the all-wheel drive system has been designed in such a way that it distributes torque through dual rear driveshafts to angled high pinion spiral bevel gears at each wheel, thus eliminating the conventional ring and pinion gear.
A Mason Motorsports differential completes the powertrain setup, running through portal gear sets mounted at each front hub – this solution was chosen so that ground clearance is maximized (we don't have the numbers on what that means).
The Passport is not your standard commercial vehicle when it comes to the chassis either. For this project, Honda and its partners opted for the Mason Gen 2 all-wheel-drive chassis that has been uniquely designed to fit the hybrid setup. That includes, among other things, a unique rear frame section meant to support the V6 engine and hybrid power unit.
Photo: Honda To maintain mass distribution, the truck's fluid tanks and batteries have been installed toward the rear of the chassis, while the 145-gallon (549 liters) carbon Kevlar safety fuel cell has been fitted at the center of the cab.
The bodywork chosen to cover all the mechanical components is made, how else, in carbon fiber, sculpted in such a way as to meet the carmaker's aerodynamic requirements. There are deep side channels behind the front wheels, the exhaust outlets have been installed high up, and they come with aerodynamic fins meant to direct exhaust flow, and tunneling solutions are included into the cab.
The truck makes the connection to the ground with Toyo tires wrapped around wheels of unspecified dimensions. Behind each of them is a suspension system that includes dual Fox Racing shocks of undisclosed capabilities.
Many of the above components and features have already proven their worth in other competitions, including Formula 1 , IndyCar, and IMSA (like, say, the F-1 trialed and tested battery pouch cells housed within a lightweight carbon-fiber case), so it's understandable why the Japanese carmaker is so hyped about all of this.
Photo: Honda Honda plans to line up the Passport Trophy truck on the starting grid for the 2027 Baja 500 race in June 2027 - it's too late for it to take part in this year's Baja 1000. In doing so, the vehicle will become the first-ever hybrid Trophy Truck to take on a SCORE World Desert Championship race. If all goes according to plan, we should also see it line up for next year's Baja 1000.
On top of that, the vehicle will also become the first to go into the competition with what Honda calls an unprecedented suite of electronics and vehicle-control technologies, including dual-axle brake-by-wire, adaptive traction control, and AI power deployment.
Behind the wheel of the monster for the truck’s first race will be two-time Baja 1000 winner Bryce Menzies, with the vehicle to race in the colors of Menzies Motorsports. The pair has a pretty huge legacy to live up to, as Honda has already scored 22 overall and 17 class victories in the Baja 1000, the most of any manufacturer taking part.
There is another aspect of the race we have to consider, and that's the fact that the 2027 iteration will also mark the race's 60th anniversary. Having a truck of this caliber taking part and potentially winning the 2027 edition adds another layer of importance to the next iteration. Naturally, we'll keep an eye on things and tell you all about it.
